fields.label: Start temp.
fields.help: Temperature at the start of this step.  If not set, the wort is assumed to be boiling.  Steps are classified as pre-boil, boil proper or post-boil by their temperatures.  For IBU formulae that model isomerization after flameout (eg mIBU and SMPH), a post-boil step that starts at boiling and ends below it is modelled as the wort cooling naturally (down to, but not below, the end temperature); any other post-boil step is modelled as the temperature changing linearly from the start temperature to the end temperature (so eg a hop stand held at 80°C (176°F) has start and end temperatures of 80°C).

fields.label: Time
fields.help: How long this step lasts, not including any ramp time.  For a post-boil step (eg whirlpool or hop stand), hops added to this step with no time set steep for this long (plus the time of any subsequent steps).

fields.label: Temp. lag time
fields.help: Ramp time: how long it takes, before this step begins, to get from the end temperature of the previous step to the start temperature of this one.  Eg, for a hop stand at 80°C (176°F), the time taken to chill the wort from boiling to that temperature.  For post-boil steps, the temperature is modelled as changing linearly during the ramp, and hops added to the step with no time set are added at the end of the ramp.  If not set, any temperature change between steps is treated as instantaneous.

fields.label: End temp.
fields.help: Temperature at the end of this step.  If not set, the wort is assumed to be boiling.

fields.label: Description
fields.help: Optional description of this boil step

fields.label: Default Batch Size
fields.help: Volume into the fermentor that new recipes using this equipment start with

fields.label: Default Pre-boil Volume
fields.help: Volume in the kettle at the start of the boil that new recipes using this equipment start with

fields.label: Total Capacity
fields.help: Total usable capacity of the mash tun, including any space below the false bottom or malt pipe

fields.label: Mash Tun Loss (not recovered)
fields.help: Liquid that stays behind in the mash tun and is never recovered

fields.label: Lauter Tun Loss (not recovered)
fields.help: Wort that stays behind in the lauter tun and is never recovered

fields.label: Total Capacity
fields.help: The most the kettle can hold (not the pre-boil volume, which is on the General tab).  If there is no separate mash tun, this is also the space available for the mash.

fields.label: Internal Diameter
fields.help: Internal diameter of the kettle at the surface of the wort.  Used, along with the opening diameter and the volume of wort in the kettle, to estimate how quickly the wort cools naturally after flameout, for IBU formulae that model isomerization after flameout (eg mIBU and SMPH).  If not set, 45 cm (about 18 inches) is assumed.

fields.label: Opening Diameter
fields.help: Internal diameter of the opening in the kettle through which steam can escape -- eg the same as the internal diameter if the kettle is uncovered, or smaller if it is partly covered.  Used, along with the internal diameter and the volume of wort in the kettle, to estimate how quickly the wort cools naturally after flameout, for IBU formulae that model isomerization after flameout (eg mIBU and SMPH).  If not set, 45 cm (about 18 inches) is assumed.

fields.label: Foundation Water (recovered)
fields.help: Water below the false bottom or malt pipe that drains out with the wort

fields.help: Percentage of this ingredient's extract that brewing yeast can ferment.  Leave blank for 100%.  Set to 0 for lactose, or about 10 for maltodextrin.  Not normally needed for malts.

fields.label: Krausen

fields.help: Free rise is used to indicate a fermentation step where the exothermic fermentation is allowed to raise the temperature without restriction

fields.label: Phenolic Off-Flavor Positive
fields.help: Whether culture is capable of producing phenols, which is a common distinctive property of saison, and brett yeasts

fields.label: Glucoamylase Positive
fields.help: A glucoamylase positive culture is capable of producing glucoamylase, the enzyme produced through expression of the diastatic gene, which allows yeast to attenuate dextrins and starches leading to a very low FG. This is positive in some saison/brett yeasts as well as the new gulo hybrid by Omega yeast labs.

fields.label: Killer Neutral
fields.help: Neutral strains do not produce toxins, nor are they killed by them
